newsitem.title: USA: G10 calls for early agreement on IMF's GAB.
newsitem.headline: G10 calls for early agreement on IMF's GAB.

text.p: The Group of Ten on Sunday welcomed progress made towards increasing emergency funds available to the International Monetary Fund but appeared to have stopped short of a final agreement on doubling these General Arrangements to Borrow (GAB).

"The ministers and governors welcomed the progress that has been made towards the establishment of New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB) and recommended that the process be brought to a rapid conclusion," the G-10 said in a statement after a meeting here on Sunday.

The G10 has long agreed in principle to double the GAB resources, used by the IMF to help countries facing serious liquidity crises, to $50 billion, but has yet to iron out exactly how this will work.
The existing GAB would be supplemented by a NAB agreement.

"Under the NAB, countries with the capacity to support the international monetary system will make supplementary resources available to the IMF to cope with an impairment of the international monetary system or to deal with an exceptional situation that poses a threat to the stability of the system," the G10 said in a statement.
"The establishment of the NAB will double the resources currently made available to the IMF under the GAB by the G10 countries," it said.

It gave no details on how this would be done, but said that the G10 "welcomed the opportunity afforded by the NAB for additional dialogue among a broader range of countries on questions of mutual interest".
Countries with emerging economies which are being asked to fund the NAB have also asked for a greater say in the running of world economic affairs in return for their contribution.
